form_name: The sub's play, run as work

cells.how: In form E, as in D, the start and the first call share one post or turn; the lines say the two coincide, and in two rooms a call came before the start.
In form E the design depends on the host and the means: a host's approval for space, the colours and size available, and the upkeep of a picture already standing.
In form E machine hands help only on conditions: their targets must match the intended image and agreed overlaps, and a changed target must reach every runner.
In form E the thread records chat invitations and claims brought back from the chat, not how the chat decided or whether planning moved there.
In form E the call and the building appear apart in the record: replies do not show that the call brought the builders, and calls recur during building (E's account, section 8).
In form E judging the hands too few ends one member's part or one expansion, not the room's place: the others keep repairing, recruit or finish, and no completed move is shown to follow.
In form E restraint answers reported harm, overlap or a contemplated enlargement, not a written attack call refused inside the room.

In form E the play is run as work: moderators start it and set its rules, real removals and bots enforce them, members test claims, repair what the styling breaks, argue its end by the clock and the time zone, and ask that its changes be kept.
In form E carrying on is invited or proposed more than taken up: a successor canvas or a reused chat is offered, and adoption, migration or continued collective work is not shown.

In form E the marking does not wait for a finished mark: rooms celebrate a recognizable or surviving emblem with planned additions unfinished, an incomplete attempt or a milestone, and pride and disappointment share the thread.

In form E the record does not wait for the celebration: timelapses, live updates and reports of loss run before any celebration, and where both appear the lines show a sequence, not that the celebration caused the record.
In form E carrying on follows the record in order only: successor invitations and reuse come after final images, but no line shows the record causing them, and uptake is not shown.

In form E the attack talk sits inside the recruiting: recruitment and attack proposals share a thread or a call, and the lines do not show that recruited builders became the attacking hands; in one room the switch ran the other way, from a rival's interference to helping the room's own mark.

changes.how: Source-code speculation within the inherited recruitment theme tests whether a teaser was a joke rather than recruiting canvas builders.
Cancellation is explained through stress, poor cooperation, reference problems and unavailable space alongside insufficient hands.
A template settles a design only with uptake and accepted authority, since repeated references and public redesigns coexist with ignored plans.
A subreddit punishment threat attempts to enforce canvas design across venue factions, without demonstrating enacted bans or technical control of pixels.
Telling keepers a revised plan is insufficient where informed factions dispute its legitimacy rather than merely misrecognizing the change as damage.
Reported chat decisions cannot be treated as room-wide consensus when nonparticipants and competing factions contest the chat's authority.
Defensive strain demonstrably elicits script requests, but limited technical knowledge prevents inferring that the requested automation actually operated.
Restraint depends on recognizing the neighbor's work and reciprocal or moral obligations, not only on knowing a coordinate boundary.
Judged incapacity can end a participant's work or one expansion project while other maintenance continues, rather than moving or ending the whole room.
Recruitment precedes attack proposals in the campaign, but the record does not establish that recruitment caused builders to turn against a rival.
A rebuilding announcement followed by a restored-picture report shows a local return to construction without making every relocation succeed.
A prospective helper asks authorization before accepting another room's assistance, a step at making terms rather than a demonstrated post-agreement representation dispute.
The record shows proposed permission-seeking and reported territorial obstacles, not durable occupancy under an agreed host authority.
Participants distinguish genuine moderation faults and functional repairs from intentional trouble obscured by the prank frame.
Members seek limits on repetitive departure jokes and retention of a useful styling change without establishing that either request was enacted.
Recipients test dates, links and hidden text while exposing prank announcements and judging whether expected tricks are worth making.
The new venue is evidenced as a destination for canvas posts, not an independently emergent pattern-following identity or negotiating collective.
Celebration and preservation coexist, but a pre-close takeover timelapse and a combined retrospective do not establish that celebration generated recording.
Members preserve prank posts and recap host stories for a returnee without necessarily recounting canvas history.
Continuation is evidenced by invitations, starts and partial work reports rather than a completed replacement monument or one unified successor target.
A successor invitation explicitly names the ended canvas as its premise, supporting closure-driven continuation independently of a preserved image.
Coalition protection concerns particular accepted works, since groups credited as allies are also accused of removing an adjacent personal inscription.
Image conversion follows a proposal but continued objections leave agreement on a final template and its construction unestablished.
A bare participation report answers the call context without establishing acceptance or a posted response from every reader.
Members test palette and scale and convert or dither a proposal before judging whether it is workable.
State reports explain the emerging image's difference from the plan while pattern checking guides ongoing restoration.
Losing an earlier drawing sends participants back into accepting a rebuilding plan rather than ending organizing.
Maintenance explains renewed permission reminders, but permission is already reported with the invitation to build in hosted space.
Shortage and reciprocal help coexist without a direct explanation that shortage caused the exchange.
Permission and reciprocal maintenance operate together while the unseen negotiation leaves the originating channel and causal sequence unresolved.
The returned denial follows reported permission within the revised ordering bound, but unseen original exchanges leave the causal mechanism unresolved.
An otherwise feasible addition still requires the host's separate approval to occupy its territory.
Achieving a recognizable logo releases promised labour for reciprocal maintenance while defense continues.
The authority denial is a participant's quotation of an opponent, not a directly observed decision binding the entire host.
The thread records a returned permission claim, not how the chat decided or whether all planning moved there.
Members repair disruptive prank styling and offer compensation for its reported practical costs.
Moderators settle the prank's cutoff by timezone while later proposals receive calendar corrections.
A late in-game prank proposal receives calendar objections without establishing an extended official licence or implemented game change.
The atlas request follows celebration without identifying celebration as its cause.
The successor invitation follows recording without stating that the record generated the plan or establishing further uptake.
A vote-threshold joke becomes a demand for a promised theme and receives confirmation of delivery.
Two turns from one author establish an invitation rather than a successful transfer of collective work.
Post-closure correction concerns omitted atlas credit while the reported image cleanup explicitly preceded lock and final external correction remains unseen.
A proposal can itself recruit helpers rather than preceding a separate recruitment stage.
Effective restraint depended on reaching placers who understood the intended design and accepted the agreement.
A published template supplied a provisional target while disagreement and attempts to limit further revision continued.
Template circulation here was coupled to chat decisions, public state reports and diplomatic instructions rather than operating independently.
The small fresh start does not establish collective evacuation, and pre-loss siting belongs to a separate process.
Participation required working invitations and public summaries for helpers unable to access the chat.
Organizers screened applicants and shared invitations privately to exclude ill-intentioned entrants and spam.
Seeing the mark brought a viewer here to confirm and contribute, but new membership and integration into ordinary routines remain unobserved.
Reported observation and diplomatic access do not establish covert infiltration, deception or secret tactical planning.
Build calls and subsequent attack calls share the room without identifying which recruited placers turned to attack.
A control disclaimer accompanied proposed terms while personal rejection followed reported terms, matching the distinction between making agreements and subsequent refusal.
Repeated repair of a planned change establishes interference, not inevitable permanent abandonment whenever informing some keepers fails.
Participants invoked the protagonist's example to justify returning space and reproach retaliatory anger.
Participants carried the takeover joke into collaborative drawing and later proposals for another prank.
Celebration and documentation are visible without a passage establishing that celebration caused the recording effort.
Documentation and continuation proposals do not establish that a record caused a successor collective effort.
Later blame follows attack calls but cannot independently establish each attacker's identity or motive.
Visible preservation and restart proposals do not establish a completed atlas entry, collective uptake or durable continuation.
Account correction directly fits the revised range, while the cleanup hope does not identify a shared copy or establish completed execution.
